newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Lockheed sees help in bid to sell UAE planes.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed sees help in bid to sell UAE planes.

text.p: The U.S. government has approved almost all the UAE's weaponry and technology requirements for F-16 fighters, a move that may help the sales bid by maker Lockheed Martin Corp, industry sources said on Sunday.

"The U.S. government has approved almost all of the UAE's requirements," Robert Lawrence, Lockheed Martin's president for Middle East and Africa, told Reuters on the sidelines of Abu Dhabi's five-day IDEX arms show that opened on Sunday.

Lockheed and France's Dassault are in a heated race to sell up to 80 warplanes to the United Arab Emirates in a long-awaited deal potentially worth $6 billion. Industry sources say the deal could be the last of its size this century.
One industry executive said the U.S. approval of most of the UAE's requirements "could help the situation" for Lockheed.
Lawrence also said the approval could boost Lockheed's bid to secure all or most of the deal.
"The Europeans have been freer in what they are willing to release," he said. "This (U.S. government approval) could help."
Markets have been rife with rumours for months that the UAE would announce its decision during IDEX, one of the world's biggest arms shows.
But Lawrence said he expected Abu Dhabi to announce its choice by the end of the year.
Industry sources said the UAE could split the package between the United States and France to safeguard political interests and diversify suppliers.
But one industry source said buying two different fighter planes could prove to be too complicated because it would require greater logistical efforts.
